# temps_oidc_provider (Resource)

An OpenID Connect identity provider people sign in to the console with. Map its groups to Temps roles with `temps_oidc_role_mapping`.

Import with `<id>`.

Required API key permissions: `settings:read`, `settings:write`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "temps_oidc_provider" "sso" {
  name          = "Company SSO"
  issuer_url    = "https://idp.example.com"
  client_id     = "temps"
  client_secret = var.oidc_client_secret
  scopes        = "openid email profile"
  enabled       = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `client_id` (String) OAuth client ID.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) OAuth client secret. Temps never returns it, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected.
- `issuer_url` (String) Issuer URL; Temps reads its discovery document.
- `name` (String) Name shown on the sign-in button.

### Optional

- `default_role` (String) Role given to users no mapping matches.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Offer the provider on the sign-in page.
- `group_claim` (String) ID-token claim holding the user's groups.
- `jit_provisioning` (Boolean) Create users on their first sign-in.
- `role_claim` (String) ID-token claim holding a role name.
- `scopes` (String) Space-separated scopes to request.
- `template` (String) Provider template the console used, for example `generic`.
- `trust_idp_email` (Boolean) Trust the email address the provider sends even if it does not mark it verified.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Import ID, `<id>`.
- `managed_by_cloud` (Boolean) Whether Temps Cloud manages the provider.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <id>
terraform import temps_oidc_provider.sso 2
```
